partsNote: index.d.ts: `export * as Tabs from './index.parts.js'`. index.parts exports exactly Root|Tab|Indicator|Panel|List. Default elements: Root=div, List=div, Tab=button, Panel=div, Indicator=span.

Root.value.semantic: controlled active value; null = no tab active

Root.defaultValue.semantic: uncontrolled initial value; default is the NUMBER 0, not undefined

Root.orientation.semantic: arrow-key axis + data-orientation; aria-orientation='vertical' is set on List only when vertical

List.activateOnFocus.semantic: false = manual activation (Enter/Space); equivalent to React Aria keyboardActivation='manual'

Tab.disabled.semantic: disabled tabs are skipped by initial selection: if the first Tab is disabled the next enabled one is selected initially — NOT during SSR, so set Root value/defaultValue to an enabled value to avoid mismatch

Tab.nativeButton.semantic: set false when render produces a non-<button> (e.g. <a>)

Panel.keepMounted.semantic: keep the closed panel in the DOM (stays hidden + inert)

Indicator.renderBeforeHydration.semantic: emits a prehydration script (package imports '#prehydration/tabs/indicator') so the indicator is positioned before hydration

allParts.semantic: className: string | (state)=>string|undefined; style: CSSProperties | (state)=>CSSProperties|undefined; render: ReactElement | (props,state)=>ReactElement; plus all native props of the default element

dataAttributes.meaning: direction of the new tab relative to the previous one (for animation)
present when the tab is active (aria-selected is also set)
present when the tab is disabled
present when the panel is hidden

renderProp: Every part takes `render`: a React element (`<Tabs.Tab render={<a href="/x" />} nativeButton={false}>`) or `(props, state) => ReactElement` where state is that part's State type (Tab {disabled, active, orientation, tabActivationDirection}; Panel {hidden, transitionStatus, orientation, tabActivationDirection}; Indicator {activeTabPosition, activeTabSize, orientation, tabActivationDirection}; Root/List {orientation, tabActivationDirection}). In function form merge with mergeProps: `render={(props, state) => <button {...mergeProps<'button'>(props, { className: styles.Tab })} />}`. For your own render-prop components use the public `useRender` hook ('@base-ui/react/use-render'). Render props nest arbitrarily. Caveat: render is for composing behaviour/props, not polymorphism; tag-specific defaults (e.g. type="button") need an explicit signal — that is what nativeButton is for.

controlled.eventDetails: { reason: 'none'|'disabled'|'missing'|'initial', event, cancel(), allowPropagation(), isCanceled, isPropagationAllowed, trigger, activationDirection }
controlled.reasonSemantics: 'none' = user-initiated (click/keyboard). 'initial' = first automatic selection/fallback when defaultValue omitted or undefined, including when the implicit initial value is disabled/missing. 'disabled' = fallback when the selected tab became disabled. 'missing' = fallback when the selected tab was removed, or an explicit defaultValue never matched a mounted tab. Automatic changes cannot be canceled (cancel() is a no-op for initial/disabled/missing).

formIntegration: None. No name/value submission, no hidden input, no Form/Field validation wiring; Root renders a plain <div>. (React Aria Tabs is not a form control either — no regression.)

keyboard.model: Roving tabindex via internals/composite: TabsList renders CompositeRoot with enableHomeAndEndKeys:true, loopFocus (prop, default true), orientation-driven axis, index-based highlight.
keyboard.keys: Arrow keys move focus along the orientation axis (Left/Right horizontal, Up/Down vertical), wrapping when loopFocus; Home/End move to first/last enabled tab (TabsList hard-enables Home/End); Enter/Space activate in manual mode. activateOnFocus={true} activates on focus, except that a secondary (non-main-button) press focuses without activating.
keyboard.typeahead: n/a (no public typeahead helper exists in the package).
keyboard.aria: List role=tablist (+aria-orientation only when vertical); Tab role=tab, aria-selected, aria-controls -> panel id, id; Panel role=tabpanel, aria-labelledby -> tab id, tabIndex 0 when open else -1, inert when closed (also when keepMounted). Only the focused tab is in the tab order.

notableDifferences: selectedKey/defaultSelectedKey/onSelectionChange (key-based) -> value/defaultValue/onValueChange; value type `any | null`, null = no active tab. Repo hit: header-navigation.tsx:204 `<Tabs selectedKey={activeTabKey}>`.
keyboardActivation='manual'|'automatic' on the root -> `activateOnFocus` boolean on Tabs.List (default false = manual). Repo uses manual (tabs/tabs.tsx:224) = default.

No `items`/collection prop on Tabs.List: React Aria takes `items` + a render child, Base UI requires explicit <Tabs.Tab> children. Repo does `<TabList items={tabItems} />` (tabs/tabs.tsx:143/205) — must expand to explicit tabs.

Render-prop state is much smaller: RAC gives {isSelected,isDisabled,isHovered,isPressed,isFocusVisible}; Base UI Tab gives only {disabled, active, orientation, tabActivationDirection}. Hover/press/focus-visible must move to CSS pseudo-classes — there is no data-hovered/data-pressed/data-focus-visible/data-selected.

Data attributes: RAC data-selected/data-hovered/data-pressed/data-focus-visible/data-disabled/data-orientation vs Base UI data-active (NOT data-selected), data-disabled, data-orientation, data-activation-direction (+ Panel data-hidden/data-index/data-starting-style/data-ending-style). REPO HAZARD: globals.css loads `@plugin "tailwindcss-react-aria-components"`, whose `selected:`/`pressed:`/`hovered:` variants key off RAC data attributes. Existing usages — table.tsx:238 `selected:bg-secondary`, button-group.tsx:26/28 `selected:`/`group-selected/`, nav-account-card.tsx:193 `pressed:` — will silently stop matching after migration. Audit these per widget (`disabled:` is native and safe).
Indicator is a first-class Base UI part (CSS vars + data-activation-direction + optional prehydration script); React Aria has none (repo hand-rolls it).
shouldForceMount -> keepMounted; Base UI closed panels are hidden + inert and keep focus out.
No public context hooks: RAC exposes TabsContext/TabsStateContext + useSlottedContext (repo uses it at tabs/tabs.tsx:115); Base UI exposes only typed Metadata/State types — prop plumbing required.
No multi-select tabs (RAC widened onChange for selectionMode='multiple'; repo already collapses arrays).
Root default active value is 0, so a Tab with value={0} is initially active if no value/defaultValue is given.
